questions.q: In a scoring script for an online endpoint, where should you load the model?
options: Inside run(), on every request
In init(), which runs once when the container starts
In a separate batch job
In the request body
questions.explain: init() runs once after the deployment is created or updated, so the model can be cached in memory. run() is called for every request and should only score.

questions.q: What is the difference between an endpoint and a deployment?
options: They are the same thing with two names
A deployment is only used for batch scoring
A deployment is the stable URL; an endpoint holds the model files
An endpoint is the stable name and authentication; deployments behind it hold the model, script, environment and compute
questions.explain: The endpoint is the stable interface callers use. Deployments are the resources that host a particular model, so you can route traffic between several of them.

questions.q: In the local test, the bad request returned HTTP 500 with a generic message. Where was the real cause, KeyError 'data', visible?
options: In the response body sent to the client
Nowhere
In the server logs
In the model registry
questions.explain: The inference server hides the exception from clients and records it in its logs. In Azure ML you read the same kind of output with get_logs or the studio Logs tab.

questions.q: Why add a green deployment with zero traffic and then mirror some traffic to it?
options: To test a new model on production requests without affecting the answers customers receive
To make the blue deployment cheaper
To skip registering the model
To switch to batch scoring
questions.explain: Mirrored traffic is copied to the green deployment; its results are not returned to clients, but metrics and logs are recorded so you can compare before shifting real traffic.

questions.q: Why should you delete a managed online endpoint when you finish practicing?
options: Endpoints expire after one hour
Deleting it retrains the model
Registered models are deleted automatically otherwise
It keeps compute allocated while it exists, so you keep paying even with no requests
questions.explain: You pay for the VMs assigned to the deployment while the endpoint exists. begin_delete removes the endpoint and all its deployments.
